thread:
natalie-support: Customer reports Private control plane mTLS failures after they rolled a firewall update around 09:10 UTC. Client connections from their VPC to our control plane are failing with TLS handshake errors. They see repeated `alert handshake_failure` in their client logs and our control plane shows no client cert presented. Can we triage?

eric-infra: Can you paste a short reproduction (curl/openssl) and any recent firewall rules they pushed? Also need a pcap of client->controlplane to inspect ClientHello.

natalie-support: Here's what the customer sent: `curl -v https://control.private.redwood:443/api/health --cert ./client.pem --key ./client.key` -> TLS handshake failed, SSL_write: error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:tlsv1 alert handshake failure. They attached a small tcpdump (first 2 packets). Uploading to case.

alice-netops: Quick suspicion: their NGFW might be doing TLS inspection (man-in-the-middle) and either stripping client certs or terminating TLS entirely. Do we see any evidence on our side of a proxied connection (SNI mismatch or missing TLS1.3 ClientHello extensions)?

eric-infra: I pulled the pcap they attached. From the ClientHello we see `server_name` is empty (SNI blank) and there's a `tls1.3` Legacy Version present but the ClientHello size looks truncated (~420 bytes). Also here's relevant openssl s_client run I asked them to run against our IP: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect 10.14.23.58:443 -tls1_3 -cert client.pem -key client.key -servername control.private.redwood
CONNECTED(00000003)
139845...:error:1417A0C2:SSL routines:tls_process_server_certificate:certificate verify failed:../ssl/statem.c:1234:
---
no peer certificate available
---
SSL handshake has read 1205 bytes and written 456 bytes
---
```

kevin-priv: If our control plane sees no client cert, that means the client's TLS session never reached our server with the client authentication step. Common causes: corporate proxy that performs TLS inspection (terminates client cert), NAT device fragmenting ClientHello, or a transparent proxy that strips TLS extensions including SNI and `signature_algorithms`.

alice-netops: Customer confirms they use Palo Alto PAN-OS 10.1 with SSL Forward Proxy enabled. They also rolled a policy change that applied decryption to all outbound TLS to `internet` from their VPC. That matches.

eric-infra: Ok probable root cause: SSL Forward Proxy is intercepting and not forwarding the client certificate chain to the origin (it terminates TLS and creates a new TLS session to us). In this mode the proxy is acting as TLS server to the client (so it sees the client cert) and then initiates a separate client connection to our control plane—there is no client cert to present to our server.

natalie-support: Customer says they *didn't* intend to break mTLS; they thought their NGFW would bypass in some CIDR ranges but rule precedence changed. They can add an allowlist, but want short-term mitigations.

eric-infra: Short term options to suggest to customer: 1) Add a no-decrypt policy for control plane IPs/hostnames so the proxy does not perform SSL inspection for these destinations. 2) If no-decrypt isn't possible, configure the proxy to forward the original client cert via TLS passthrough (some appliances support SSL passthrough instead of interception). 3) Move control plane traffic to a dedicated port that bypasses decryption rules (if their appliance supports rule by port).

alice-netops: For PAN-OS example they should use a Decryption Policy with action = no-decrypt for destination `control.private.redwood` and ensure it sits above any general decrypt rule. Example high-level rule: 
```
rule: bypass-control-plane
source: VPC_SUBNETS
destination: control.private.redwood
service: application-default
action: no-decrypt
position: before general-decrypt
```

kevin-priv: Also ask them to validate the full client cert chain. If the client only has an end-entity cert without intermediate CAs, some proxies may fail to forward properly. Have them run: 
```
openssl verify -CAfile chain.pem client.pem
```

eric-infra: Capture checklist we need from customer to escalate if they can't change proxy rules: 
- Packet capture (pcap) showing initial TCP handshake + ClientHello (first 1-2 seconds).
- Output of `openssl s_client -connect <CP_IP>:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -servername control.private.redwood -state -msg`
- NGFW config snippet for SSL/Decryption policy and the exact rule they changed.
- Any TLS inspection cert installed in their endpoint trust store (screenshot of cert chain in browser).

natalie-support: Customer attached full pcap now. I see two TLS handshakes in the pcap: client<->proxy, proxy<->controlplane. Proxy's client->controlplane handshake uses a different ClientHello (no client auth extensions). So this is definitely interception.

eric-infra: Recommended support reply to customer (copy/paste): 
"Our control plane requires end-to-end TLS with client certificate authentication. Your NGFW's SSL Forward Proxy is terminating TLS and therefore the client certificate is not being forwarded to our servers. Please configure a no-decrypt/bypass rule for traffic to control.private.redwood (or enable TLS passthrough). After applying the rule, capture a fresh pcap and confirm the ClientHello reaches our control plane with SNI set to control.private.redwood and client auth extensions present. If you cannot change the NGFW config, we can schedule a troubleshooting call with your network team and our infra engineers."

kevin-priv: I'm available to join a call. Also note for longer-term: we'll document recommended firewall rules in the Private deployment onboarding guide (add a section on SSL Forward Proxy bypass).

infra-bot: :white_check_mark: Support case updated (#CASE-2026). Escalation flagged to infra on-call.

natalie-support: Customer replied they will test a no-decrypt rule in their staging VPC and report back within 2 hours. Marking this thread pending. :thumbsup:
